Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — latency targets and autoscale questions

Thanks for the call earlier, Ethan and Lina — good to meet you both. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have alignment before the technical sync: 

Summary of FastPay requirements (from today):
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for streaming chat responses (user-visible token streaming)
- Throughput: baseline 600 reqs/min with spikes up to 2,400 reqs/min during promotions
- Concurrency: up to 180 concurrent sessions, average session length ~45s
- Streaming: need sub-100ms first-byte for streaming start, then steady streaming at ~20-40ms per chunk

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Autoscale scale-up time for burst from baseline to peak and whether warm pools reduce tail latency
2) Queueing behavior when warm pools are exhausted — how requests are buffered and SLA implications
3) Recommended warm pool size & pre-warmed instance types for your traffic profile
4) Any constraints for your PCI environment we should know for private deployment

Attached: FastPay-SLO-worksheet.xlsx (your inputs + our initial sizing) and Redwood-autoscale-proposal.pdf (initial recommendations).

Next steps:
- Marissa: follow up with sizing & warm pool recommendation (this thread) — by EOD tomorrow
- Technical sync: Rishi + Hannah + FastPay infra team — propose Wed 7/14 10am PT (please confirm)
- FastPay: share any historical 1-minute cadence traffic (last 30 days) if possible

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

- Buffering: we prefer limited queuing (max 10s) over instant rejection; user experience during checkout is sensitive.
- We can provide 1-min cadence traffic for last 90 days; I’ll share a redacted CSV.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency targets and autoscale questions

Appreciate the clarifications, Ethan. A few practical notes from the serving/ops side so the technical sync is productive: 

1) Warm pools & scale-up times
- Warm pool (pre-warmed GPU-backed vCPU containers) typically reduce scale-up tail by ~30–60s depending on instance type and model KV-cache size.
- From cold: full scale + model load and KV-cache warm can take ~120–300s for large models (Llama-2-large style).
- We recommend a warm pool sized for ~20–25% of expected spike concurrency to keep p99 reasonably bounded. For your 180 concurrent sessions peak, that suggests 36–45 warm workers.

2) Queueing behavior & backpressure
- By default Redwood uses a short request buffer (configurable) with max buffer time; requests older than buffer age will be rejected with a 429. For ecomm we can configure a 10s buffer as you requested.
- We can stream partial responses while the backend is catching up (useful for chat/checkout flows) — first-byte policy configurable to favor low FBT (first byte time).

3) Burst capacity & pricing implications
- Burst capacity (auto-burst to shared-hosted capacity or reserved burst for Dedicated) can be used for infrequent promotions. We'll outline cost tradeoffs in the proposal PDF.

4) Telemetry we need before the sync
- 1-min cadence QPS, p95/p99 latency per minute if available, and any peak window traces for past promotions.

I’ll bring a short runbook and suggested warm pool sizes to the sync. Marissa, I put a note on pricing options for reserved bursts — happy to join the call.

—Rishi
